persistence_invariants.brief: (sku, location) is unique; no two stock records share this pair (R3)
Picks are atomic; no allocation can exceed available quantity, preventing double-allocation (R2)
created_at is NOT NULL and immutable; every record has an unmodifiable timestamp (R1)
created_by is NOT NULL and immutable; every record tracks the actor who made it (R1)
Migrations are additive; existing stock records survive every schema iteration without loss (R1)

nfrs.brief: Schema migrations are additive; existing stock records and all created data survive every schema iteration without loss
Every inventory adjustment records an immutable timestamp (created_at) and actor (created_by); these fields are unmodifiable post-creation
Stock levels never drop below zero; any operation that would create negative inventory is rejected at write time with a clear error
No pick can allocate beyond available quantity; concurrent allocations that would overcommit are rejected atomically at write time
Each (sku, location) pair is uniquely addressable; no two stock records share this combination. Collisions are resolved at write time

Integration tests run against the paired Lakebase branch with live database state; mocked or in-memory substitutes are forbidden. CI refuses to merge PRs whose integration tests don't run against a real branch

The frontend is a React + TypeScript SPA under client/; the backend returns JSON only. Warehouse-floor tablet loads the app once and navigates client-side with no full-page reloads; stock adjustments update affected rows in place (optimistic + reconciliation)
Validation error messages are clear and specific, naming the offending field (not generic 'bad request')
Stock-level rows with missing optional detail (par level, batch, serial) render cleanly with explicit 'not tracked' labels; never null crashes or blank regions
Barcode-scan interactions feel immediate; perceived response under ~200ms from scan event to UI update
